title: Effects vs event handlers: who does what?

slides.text: Not render. Not a click. Then what? 🤔
slides.say: Some code isn't about drawing the screen, and no click caused it. So where does it go? Let's find out.

slides.text: Rendering calculates the UI. Event handlers run when the user does something.
slides.say: Rendering code only calculates what to show. Event handlers run when the user does something, like clicking a button.

slides.text: Effects run because the component was shown, not because of a click.
slides.say: Effects are the third kind. They run because the component appeared on screen, no matter which interaction led there.
Staying connected to the chat should happen whenever the room is shown, so it is an effect. Sending a message happens because of one click, so it lives in the event handler.

slides.text: Effects are for syncing with an external system: a server, a timer, a browser API.
slides.say: Use effects to step outside React and sync with an external system. If there's no external system, you probably don't need one.
So remember: caused by being shown, use an effect. Caused by a click, use an event handler.
